Name: Energy Efficiency
Summary: Ecotect simulations of 768 residential building shapes, pairing eight geometry and glazing features with heating load and cooling load targets.
Description:
The Energy Efficiency dataset relates the heating load and cooling load requirements of buildings to their design parameters. Its creators are Athanasios Tsanas and Angeliki Xifara, and it was donated to the UCI Machine Learning Repository in 2012, with their paper on estimating the energy performance of residential buildings with statistical machine learning tools, published in Energy and Buildings, vol. 49.

The data comes from energy analysis of 12 different building shapes simulated in Ecotect. Varying the glazing area, glazing area distribution, orientation and other parameters gives 768 building shapes. Each of the 768 samples has eight features: relative compactness, surface area, wall area, roof area, overall height, orientation, glazing area and glazing area distribution.

The eight features are used to predict two real-valued responses, heating load (y1) and cooling load (y2); rounding a response to the nearest integer turns it into a multi-class classification problem. There are no missing values. The data ships as one 74.4 KB Excel file, ENB2012_data.xlsx, under CC BY 4.0.
